correctness.rationale: The first force needs its source and at least degree minus b already-black neighbors, giving max(1, minimum degree minus b plus 1); an initially all-black graph meets this bound as well. The endpoint of a nonsaturated path power fills its closed neighborhood from the stated initial segment, after which successive black vertices one at a time force the next vertex. On a nonsaturated cycle the chosen source's radius-k interval contains the entire seed, and its force fills a block of length 2k+1. A black vertex k-1 positions before the right endpoint sees only the next white vertex outside a block of that length or greater, so propagation reaches the entire cycle. Complete powers reduce to the white count at any black vertex. Independent exhaustive closure enumeration for paths of orders 2–9, cycles of orders 3–9, powers 1–7 and thresholds 1 through minimum degree plus 2 agreed in 589 profiles over 21493 candidate seeds. evidence: Let d be a positive minimum degree and suppose an ordinary zero-forcing seed S has size d. At its first force the black source u has exactly one white neighbor and at most d-1 black neighbors. Necessarily deg(u)=d and S is contained in N[u]. Thus N[u] is itself an ordinary forcing set, by monotonicity in the black set.

For any b, start with u and max(0,d-b) of its neighbors. Its first b-force fills N[u], and the remaining ordinary sequence works by skipping any targets already black. Hence Z_b=max(1,d-b+1) by the prior lower bound. Proposition 7 gives the hypothesis for nonsaturated paths and Proposition 8 does so for nonsaturated cycles. Observation 2.2 gives the saturated cases.
